A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices for the same benchmark paper, renamed from PlanQA to FloorplanQA. The substantial revision supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 11 LLMs on synthetic layouts, encoding and perturbation ablations, and additional image-assisted experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 15 LLMs on synthetic and HSSD layouts, semantic ablations, layout-complexity analysis and token-truncation results.

M1.justification: The benchmark pipeline gains HSSD projection, object filtering and hull-based geometry cleanup, with a unified polygonal representation replacing the stated flat bounding-box inputs (Sections 3.2–3.4). Max Box changes from axis-aligned search to optimization over rectangle orientations (v1 Table 11; v2 Appendix G.8). These are procedural adaptations, beyond renaming or additional evaluation alone.

E1.justification: v2 adds 200 HSSD layouts with additional room types and irregular, rotated geometry alongside the retained synthetic kitchens, bedrooms and living rooms. Area and Missing Object tasks and the image-assisted input scenario disappear; Max Box now permits rotation. Distance/Pair Distance, Fit/Placement/Placement and Obstruction/Visibility are matched across renaming.

E2.justification: The main comparison changes from 11 to 15 models, adding GPT-5, GPT-OSS, Claude Sonnet 4, Kimi-K2 and Devstral while removing Llama, Gemma, Phi and DeepSeek-V3 comparators. DeepSeek-R1 is updated to R1-0528. Encoding and prompt ablations replace GPT-4.1, GPT-4o-mini and DeepSeek-R1 with GPT-OSS-120B, GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-235B-A22B (v1 Tables 5 and 9; v2 Tables 3 and 8).

E3.justification: Reported token limits change from 8,192 for reasoning models and 4,096 for others to 12,288 for large models and 8,192 for mid-size models, with GPT-5 exceptions. v2 specifies temperature zero except GPT-5 and adds checklist/error-response requirements. Free Space tolerance changes from 2% to 5%, and completed-answer-only accuracy becomes an additional metric (Sections 3.4–3.6; Appendix I).

E4.justification: v2 adds geometry-preserving semantic-label permutation, HSSD Free Space accuracy versus object/overlap counts, and detailed truncation analyses (Appendices E–I; Figure 11). Case studies expand from two task-specific failure discussions to eight. The coordinate-jitter ablation and JSON-versus-JSON-plus-image study are removed; encoding and object-reference ablations remain under revised comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive means and standard deviations across model/task/room groups and state that generation seeds accompany the code. v2 adds no evaluation repeat counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Completion-only accuracy changes the evaluation metric, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The accuracy matrices are extensively replaced. GPT-4.1 kitchen Distance is reported as 100% in v1 versus 96.5% in v2, and bedroom Free Space as 2.8% versus 31.2% (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 6). These are revised-setting results, not controlled performance changes. HSSD, semantic-ablation and truncation results are added, while Area, Missing Object, jitter and image-assisted result entries disappear.

T1.justification: Task mathematics changes locally: View Angle becomes the angle to global north instead of a facing-vector comparison, and Max Box is formalized as maximizing area over orientations (v2 Appendices G.4 and G.8). Existing layout-validity inequalities remain. No new theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from failure to generalize under layout perturbation to mostly robust behavior under small spatial perturbations. The conclusion drops the approximately 30B-parameter plateau claim and replaces modest reasoning-model gains with notable Free Space/Max Box benefits. The contribution also expands to an HSSD-based realism check (abstract, introduction and Section 5).

C2.justification: v2 develops task-specific explanations involving polygon-centroid arithmetic, missed geometric unions and rotation errors, and interprets semantic-label sensitivity as reliance on linguistic priors (Appendices F–G). It expands the discussion of token limits and interprets completed-only accuracy as an approximate upper bound. v1's interpretations and limitations concerning visual grounding and floorplan-image variability disappear.

D1.justification: v2 documents HSSD exclusion categories, projection cleanup and geometry operations, adds explicit response/error schemas, and expands ground-truth implementation descriptions, including Shapely union operations and orientation search (Appendices C, G and H). Supplementary-code, prompt and seed disclosures remain, but v1's direct project-page link is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds HSSD, alpha-hull/alpha-shape and Shapely references and citations for newly evaluated model families, while removing references associated with dropped comparators. Section 2 largely retains the positioning against visual, embodied and layout-generation benchmarks; the research-positioning narrative is not substantially rewritten.

P1.justification: Beyond the PlanQA-to-FloorplanQA rename, v2 substantially rewrites the method exposition, results and conclusion, and replaces five cognitive clusters with three reasoning categories. The appendices are reorganized, with the earlier taxonomy table and selected failure discussions recast into a consistent task-definition, ground-truth and failure-analysis structure.

P2.justification: v2 redraws layout examples, replaces the cognitive heatmap/model-size presentation with grouped general/reasoning charts, splits the main accuracy matrix into two tables and reorganizes radar plots. It adds HSSD cleanup, object-distribution and complexity figures plus truncation tables, replaces failure illustrations, and changes the document template and typography.

improvement.justification: HSSD coverage and more detailed geometric explanations strengthen relevance and diagnosis. However, the new truncation control is unreliable: Table 13 repeats 35 of 36 numerical rows from overall-accuracy Table 7 despite substantial truncation in Table 12, and Table 11 appears to swap Claude/GPT-4.1 Visibility results. The jitter experiment also disappears while the abstract asserts spatial-perturbation robustness. These substantive benefits and new evidence-reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
